Interesting! Clicking the dot at (45,18) — the token moved from (50-52, 11-13) to (44-46, 17-19). It jumped 2 dots' worth (from center (51,12) to (45,18)) — skipping over the dot at (49,14). Did the dot at (49,14) disappear? The diff doesn't show (49,14) changing from G to B... let me check: the diff only shows the token's move and the timer. So the dot at (49,14) still exists? The new token is at (44-46, 17-19), which covers the dot at (45,18). The dot at (49,14) should still be there.
Wait, but in the previous move: I clicked (51,12) and the token moved from (53,10) to (51,12) — exactly to the clicked dot. So the rule is: clicking any trail dot teleports the token to that dot (anywhere on the trail?). Hmm, or maybe the token can only move to dots within a certain range? (51,12)→(45,18) is a jump of 6 rows.
Actually, the rule might be simpler: clicking a dot moves the token to that dot. So I could click the last dot (17,46) and jump straight to the end of the trail! Then one more click to reach the ball?
But wait — the earlier click on the ball (14,49) did nothing, and the click on the purple square (59,4) also did nothing. The ball isn't a dot, so it can't be clicked as a target. The purple square was the token itself.
So the plan: click the dot at (17,46) (the last dot before the ball). Then the token will be at (16-18, 45-47), adjacent to the ball. Then... how does the token reach the ball? Maybe once the token is adjacent, the level is cleared? Or do I need to click the ball? Clicking the ball earlier did nothing (when the token was far away). Maybe when the token is adjacent, clicking the ball completes the level.
Hmm, but wait — is the goal to reach the ball, or is the ball an obstacle? The purple square in the HUD (4-6, 30-32) might be a "target color" indicator: the token is purple, the HUD shows purple — consistent with the token being the player.
Or maybe the goal is: the ball rolls to the token? The ball has a gray core... the trail dots are gray (G). The ball's core is G. Hmm.
Anyway let's proceed: click (17,46), then observe. If the token teleports there, then try clicking the ball's center (14,49) to complete.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether the token can jump to any dot. The two observed moves: (53,10)→(51,12) [1 dot ahead], then (51,12)→(45,18) [3 dots ahead]. Both were to the clicked dot. So yes, it teleports to the clicked dot.
Timer: currently 58px → 29 actions remaining. Plenty.
Plan: batch: click (17,46), then click the ball (14,49). But if the first click completes something or changes the state, the second click might be wrong. Safer: click (17,46), observe, then decide.
